# RCA: downtime dispatcher sends nothing in cheap mode despite 2–3 idle slots

## Symptom

In cheap mode the local llama-proxy reports 3 slots with 2–3 idle for extended periods, yet the
herdr downtime dispatcher produces no dispatches. Observed in the window immediately before the
proxy was switched to fast mode (2026-09-19 ~00:13Z).

## Evidence (llama-proxy status log, proxy clock = UTC+1)

Source: `GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/logs/tail?source=proxy&lines=100000` (log file starts at
proxy 00:00 = UTC 23:00 on 2026-09-18).

- Window proxy 01:01–01:12 = **UTC 00:01–00:12**: `mode=cheap`, `total_slots=3`,
  `available_slots=2` (constant — 2 slots idle), and **zero** dispatches in
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- `local_owner_session_id = ["http://localhost:8080","herdr-1789775322-722064-10708"]` — the owner
  is a **dispatched downtime pane** (`Downtime triggered implement … CG-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1`), whose
  local dispatch lease ran 836s → 0 across the window (`local_active_query=true` throughout).
- Across the whole UTC 23:00–04:11 log: **56%** of status samples had ≥2 idle slots **and** an
  active lease; **10%** had all slots idle **and** an active lease.

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()`:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
const contentionQueueDepth = ...;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
if (contentionQueueDepth > 0) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

This gate runs **before** the coordination file is read, is **machine-wide**, and has **no per-slot
branch** — it fires even in per-slot mode (`requiredFreeSlots=1 < total=3`). While any dispatched
agent is alive and holds the shared local-dispatch lease, the dispatcher refuses to dispatch at
all, leaving the remaining unowned free slots unused. In cheap mode a single long-running agent
therefore monopolises the dispatcher's permission for the whole generation (adaptive lease up to
`local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds`, default 1500s; observed 840s).

The code comment claims the gate is only a single-slot (count-based) fallback superseded by per-slot
identity, and that leases expire in ~180s. Both assumptions are false for this deployment.

## Contributing causes

1. **Owner-signal schema drift** — the proxy serves `local_owner_session_id` as a JSON **array**;
   `parseLlamaStatus` expects a **string** and silently drops it, so the worker cannot identify the
   owning slot/session and falls back to `lease_remaining > 0`.
2. **No queue-depth signal** — `contention_queue_depth` is not served in this configuration.
3. **Header vs proxy UI disagree** — the herdr header only shows idle when *all* slots are idle,
   while the proxy UI shows `available_slots`; "idle slots but no dispatches" is invisible in herdr.
4. **Scheduler targets the affected window** — the mode scheduler is `[('01:00','cheap'),('10:00','fast')]`,
   so the overnight window is precisely the one this gate wastes.

## Goal

Restore cheap-mode overnight throughput by removing the machine-wide dispatch block, aligning the
owner-lease contract, and making the gate decision observable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. In cheap mode with ≥1 unowned free slot, a dispatched agent holding a lease no longer prevents
   dispatch (measured: dispatches resume during agent runs).
2. The proxy owner-lease payload is parsed without silent data loss and covered by a contract test.
3. The dispatcher records *why* it did not dispatch (`slotOwned` / `contention` / `no-candidate` /
   `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze`) to `downtime-coordination.log` and the header.
4. The lease-TTL assumption in `downtime-worker.ts` matches the proxy's adaptive-lease behaviour.

## Related work items

Children cover each fix; see the child items of this RCA.

- **WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6** – Client-side compaction response to llm-proxy compaction gate (cheap hard-cap 4xx) (completed)

# Make the downtime owner-lease gate per-slot

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

In cheap mode (3 slots) the downtime dispatcher must keep dispatching into **unowned free slots**
even while another dispatched agent holds the shared local-dispatch lease. Today it dispatches
nothing for the whole duration of any agent run, wasting 2–3 slots.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()` applies a **machine-wide** gate before reading the
coordination file:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

There is no per-slot branch — it fires even when `requiredFreeSlots < total_slots` (per-slot mode).
So a single working agent that holds a lease blocks all dispatch, despite `countFreeUnownedSlots`
reporting free slots. Evidence: proxy UTC 00:01–00:12, cheap mode, `total_slots=3`,
`available_slots=2`, lease held by a dispatched pane, **zero dispatches**.

The gate's comment claims it is only the count-based (single-slot) fallback and is superseded by
per-slot identity. That is not what the code does.

## Required behaviour

- Detect per-slot mode from the status (`Array.isArray(status.slots)` and a usable slot array).
- In per-slot mode, allow dispatch while `countFreeUnownedSlots(status.slots) >= <tier minimum>`;
  the global owner lease must not block dispatch into free unowned slots.
- Keep the conservative gate only for the count-based (single-slot / no per-slot data) path, so a
  truly owned sole slot is still protected.
- Never dispatch into a slot whose per-slot `owner_session_id` is set.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: per-slot status with 3 slots, 1 owned/busy and 2 free unowned, a held global lease,
   and `runningPanes > 0` → dispatch **proceeds** (regression test for this RCA).
2. Unit test: count-based status (no `slots`), `local_lease_active`/owner held, `runningPanes > 0`
   → dispatch is **refused** (single-slot protection preserved).
3. Unit test: per-slot status where every slot is owned → dispatch refused.
4. Audit-tier minimum (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`) is evaluated against the per-slot
   unowned-free count.
5. Integration/manual evidence: in cheap mode, dispatches are observed in `downtime-dispatches.log`
   while a previously dispatched agent is still `working`.

## Notes

- `countFreeUnownedSlots` and `isSlotOwned` already exist and exclude owned slots.
- Do not weaken the single-slot path: an owned sole slot must still block.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: owner-lease gate must be per-slot (slotOwned blocks dispatch despite free slots)

# parseLlamaStatus: accept the proxy's array local_owner_session_id (+ per-slot owner contract test)

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Stop silently dropping the proxy's local-owner signal so the dispatcher can reason about ownership
per slot instead of falling back to `lease_remaining > 0`.

## Problem

The llama-proxy now serves `local_owner_session_id` as a JSON **array**, e.g.:

```json
"local_owner_session_id": ["http://localhost:8080", "herdr-1789775322-722064-10708"],
"local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds": 29.99
```

`parseLlamaStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:838`) accepts only a **string**:

```ts
local_owner_session_id: typeof o.local_owner_session_id === 'string' ? o.local_owner_session_id : undefined,
```

The array is dropped → `ownerLeaseHeld`'s string clause is dead code, and the worker cannot tell
which session (or slot) holds the lease. This blocks the per-slot fix (WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28 child).

## Required behaviour

- Parse both shapes: legacy string and the current array. Normalise to a stable internal form
  (e.g. `local_owner_session_ids: string[]`) while keeping the legacy `string` field for
  compatibility with existing call sites.
- Fail-closed on an unparseable owner value (treat as ambiguous → busy), consistent with the rest
  of the parser.
- Keep per-slot `owner_session_id` parsing as-is (already string|null).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: legacy payload (`local_owner_session_id` string) parses and preserves the owner.
2. Unit test: current payload (2-element array) parses; the owner session is recovered (not
   `undefined`) and the URL element is ignored/handled deterministically.
3. Unit test: malformed owner (number/object/empty array) → fail-closed (busy / undefined), no throw.
4. A contract test pins the exact array shape observed from the live proxy
   (`["http://localhost:8080", "<session-id>"]`).
5. `fetchLocalStatus` never throws on either shape (poller result is a valid `LlamaStatus` or null).

## Notes

- Capture the fixture from `GET /llama/local/status`; the array shape was observed on
  2026-09-19 with proxy mode `cheap`, `total_slots=3`.
data.title: Herdr parseLlamaStatus: accept array local_owner_session_id from llama-proxy (+ per-slot owner contract test)

# Log the dispatcher's actual no-dispatch reason (make gate decisions observable)

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Make it possible to diagnose "idle slots but no dispatches" from the logs alone. This RCA took hours
because the gate decision was invisible: the only persisted outcomes are successful dispatches and
3-strike errors.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()` returns neutral outcomes for several blockers
without recording *why*:

- `slotOwned` → `{ polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true }` (no log)
- `contentionQueueDepth > 0` → same (no log)
- `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` / `fresh-audit-skip` / `audit-in-flight`
- the idle-duration gate not yet met (`polled: true, idle: true`)

The herdr header only distinguishes dispatching / off / paused / idle / busy, and idle only shows
when *all* slots are idle (per-slot tracker). There is no record of `slotOwned` blocking dispatch,
so the proxy UI shows idle slots while the dispatcher is refusing.

## Required behaviour

- On each tick that polls and does not dispatch, append a structured entry to
  `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (or a dedicated decision log) with: outcome reason, free
  slot count / total slots, owner present, `runningPanes`, contention depth, and tick timestamp.
- Rate-limit / de-duplicate so a healthy idle loop does not flood the log (e.g. log on reason
  change or at most once per N minutes per instance).
- Surface the current blocking reason in the worklist header (extend `renderDowntimeStatus`, e.g.
  `[downtime held: slot-owner]`) without changing the existing state labels.
- Do not log on every 10s tick while genuinely idle-and-eligible (no candidate vs gate-blocked are
  distinct): only record actionable refusals.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A tick refused by `slotOwned` writes one decision log line containing the reason and the
   observed slot/owner fields.
2. A tick refused by `contentionQueueDepth > 0` writes the reason and depth.
3. Repeated identical refusals are rate-limited (bounded lines per hour) — asserted by test.
4. The header shows the active blocking reason distinct from plain `idle`/`busy`.
5. Existing dispatch/error log schemas are unchanged (additive only); all consumers/tests updated.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: log the actual no-dispatch reason (slotOwned/contention/no-candidate) + header

# Re-verify the local dispatch-lease TTL assumption; exclude leases held by our own panes

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Align the dispatcher's owner-lease model with what the proxy actually does, so the gate is neither
over- nor under-conservative.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` documents and relies on the assumption that local proxy
leases "expire ~180 s after activity stops". Observation from the live proxy contradicts this:
during UTC 00:01–00:12 a dispatched pane's lease was `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`
**836 → 0** (≈840 s), i.e. an order of magnitude longer than the code assumes. The proxy
(`llm-manager` `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`) computes an **adaptive** lease with
`local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds` defaulting to 1500 s, plus chunk/prefill refresh buffers. So a
long agent generation holds the lease for its whole run.

Consequence: any gate keyed on "lease held" blocks for the entire generation, not ~3 minutes.
This amplifies the `slotOwned` defect (the per-slot fix is the primary remedy; this item removes the
stale assumption and the self-blocking case).

## Required behaviour

- Re-read the proxy lease semantics (static + adaptive + refresh buffers) and document the real
  bounds in `downtime-worker.ts`, replacing the "~180 s" claim.
- If the dispatcher spawns a pane, it knows that pane's session id; a lease held by one of the
  dispatcher's own live panes must not be treated as "someone else owns the target slot"
  (it already owns its slot, not the free ones).
- Keep fail-closed behaviour when the proxy serves no lease information.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The lease-TTL comment/constant in `downtime-worker.ts` reflects the proxy's actual maximum
   (adaptive lease max), with a unit test bounding the waited-out/refusal behaviour.
2. A lease attributable to a dispatcher-spawned pane does not block dispatch into other unowned
   free slots (test).
3. No regression: a lease held by an unknown/operator session on a count-based single-slot setup
   still blocks dispatch.
4. `docs/` (or the module header) records the proxy lease contract and the cross-repo dependency
   (`llm-manager`), so the assumption does not silently drift again.

## Notes

- Cross-repo: the lease implementation lives in `llm-manager` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`).
  If that repo changes the defaults, this item's constant must be revisited.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: correct local dispatch-lease TTL assumption; do not block on leases held by own panes

# Wire up interview command to shortcut chord

## Problem statement

Herdr's `r` key is currently a single-key Producer Review shortcut. Convert it to a prefix key, adding `r-p` (Producer Review) and `r-i` (`wl interview`) as two-key chords — enabling a consistent `r`-prefix axis for work-item review workflows.

## Users

- **Map** (agent operator): Wants faster access to interview mode for work items with outstanding producer review questions, via a consistent `r` prefix axis alongside other work-item management chords (e.g. `a` for audit, `u` for update, `x` for close).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `r` key is converted from a single-key shortcut to a prefix key with two children:
   - `r-p`: Runs Producer Review (the existing single-key command moved to chord)
   - `r-i`: Runs `wl interview <id>` to walk through outstanding interview questions on the selected work item
2. No existing shortcut functionality is lost — Producer Review still works via `r-p`.
3. The shortcut hints in the help line correctly display `r-p: Producer Review` and `r-i: interview` when `r` is pressed as a prefix.
4. All existing shortcut chords (audit `a-*`, update `u-*`, filter `f-*`, etc.) remain unaffected.

5. At least one automated test validates the new `r-p` and `r-i` chords (e.g. a `shortcut-config` unit test asserting both chords resolve to the expected commands).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- This is a configuration-only change in `shortcuts.json`; no code changes needed.
- The chord system already supports multi-key chords (e.g. `a,a`, `u,p,l`), so no changes to `shortcut-config.ts` are required.

## Existing state

- `shortcuts.json` entry for `r`: single-key chord running `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add <id> --body '<producer_comment>' --author <author>` (Producer Review).
- The chord system in `shortcut-config.ts` already supports arbitrary-length chords and leader-key prefix lookups via `getChordByLeader()`.

## Desired change

- Replace the single-key `r` entry with two two-key entries:
  - `r-p`: `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add <id> --body '<producer_comment>' --author <author>`
  - `r-i`: `!!wl interview <id>`
- Remove `r` as a single-key shortcut.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — chord registry; edit to replace `r` entry with `r-p` and `r-i` entries

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: This is narrowly scoped to shortcuts.json. Adding more `r`-prefix chords (e.g. `r-n` for intake, `r-s` for ship) are out of scope but could be follow-up work items.
- **Breaking change**: The `r` single-key shortcut is removed; users who relied on `r` for quick Producer Review must use `r-p` instead.
- **Assumption**: The chord system's prefix handling in `shortcut-config.ts` already works correctly when a single-key entry is replaced by two-key entries starting with the same key — no code changes needed.

## Related work

- WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O — Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides
- WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR — Herdr: add/remove/edit inline notes on any markdown document (adds `n-e` and `n-d` chords)

## Clarifying questions and answers

1. Q: Should `r` become a prefix only (removing single-key Producer Review), or use a different prefix key? — A: `r` becomes prefix only (option a). The work item description explicitly states "Make r a prefix key" and "r-p: Move the existing Producer Review command to r chord". Source: work item description + code inspection.
2. Q: Should the interview command be `!!wl interview <id>` (shell) or `/herdr:interview <id>` (agent command)? — A: `!!wl interview <id>`. The interview command is a `wl` subcommand, not a `/herdr:` agent command, so it must be a shell command. Source: `wl --help` inspection.

data.description:
# Intake Brief: Client retry does not honor Retry-After (503 startup_ramp)

## Problem statement

The llm-proxy's **post-restart startup ramp** gate returns HTTP `503` with a
randomized `Retry-After` header (5-18 s) and a machine-readable body
(`{"error":{"type":"startup_ramp","code":"startup_ramp","message":"Server is starting up; retry shortly."},"status":503,"retry_after":N}`)
specifically so that clients spread their reconnects across the ramp window
(`startup_ramp.max_seconds: 180` in `proxy/config.yaml`; proxy side tracked as
LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX).

The Pi client does **not** honor that hint. Its *agent-level* auto-retry
(`getRetrySettings()` -> `retryDelayMs() = baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`,
`baseDelayMs` default 2000 ms, cap 60 000 ms, **no jitter**) ignores both the
`Retry-After` header and the `retry_after` body field.

### Evidence (2026-09-20)

Proxy restarted at 16:11:28 local; the 180 s startup ramp was active until
~16:14:28. Session `herdr-1789917126-2590234-11663` (model `plan`, provider
`Local Proxy`), every turn failing with
`503: {"type":"startup_ramp",...}`:

| attempt | time (local) | gap vs prev |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| 1       | 16:12:10.5   | -           |
| 2       | 16:12:12.6   | +2.0 s      |
| 3       | 16:12:16.6   | +4.0 s      |
| 4       | 16:12:24.6   | +8.0 s      |
| 5       | 16:12:40.7   | +16.0 s     |
| 6       | 16:13:12.8   | +32.1 s     |
| 7       | 16:14:13.1   | +60.3 s     |

This is exactly `2000 * 2^(attempt-1)` capped at 60 000 ms - the client's own
deterministic backoff, independent of the `Retry-After` values the proxy
returned (random randint in [5,15] + 3 s margin per request, logged by the
proxy as `Startup ramp: deferring chat request (... retry_after=Ns)`).

A second session (`herdr-1789917234-2590706-9592`, this very analysis session)
shows the same `+2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0` pattern.

## Impact

1. Clients retry **sooner than instructed** (e.g. `Retry-After: 7` -> retry at
   2 s), hammering the freshly restarted proxy - the opposite of the ramp's
   intent.
2. Backoff has **no jitter**, so clients that started together retry in
   lockstep, defeating the ramp's desynchronisation goal.
3. The retry cap (`maxAgentDelayMs` 60 s) is shorter than the ramp window (up
   to 180 s), so a client can exhaust its retry budget mid-ramp and surface a
   hard failure to the user even though the server said "retry shortly".

## Users

- Operators/developers running herdr workers (Pi agents) against the local
  llm-proxy.
- Anyone whose first provider request after a mode switch / proxy restart lands
  inside the ramp window.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: When an OpenAI-compatible provider response carries `Retry-After`
  (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) and the request is retried, the client's delay is
  at least the server-requested delay (bounded by a configurable maximum,
  default 60 s).
- **AC2**: The `503 startup_ramp` body's `retry_after` field is honored as a
  fallback when the header is absent or unparseable.
- **AC3**: Missing/malformed hints fall back to the existing exponential
  backoff, unchanged.
- **AC4**: A client can survive a full startup ramp (up to
  `startup_ramp.max_seconds`, default 180 s) without exhausting its retry budget,
  or the ramp window is otherwise communicated so a long ramp does not surface
  as a final user-visible failure solely because the retry budget ran out first.
- **AC5**: Jitter is applied to (or combined with) any delay derived from the
  server hint so concurrent clients do not retry in lockstep.
- **AC6**: Tests cover header/body parsing, the cap, malformed values, and the
  long-ramp case; full suite green.
- **AC7**: No double-retry amplification between the provider-level and
  agent-level retry layers.

## Constraints

- Tracked in ContextHub; the change belongs in the **Pi coding agent codebase**
  (same arrangement as WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO).
- Pi already exposes a provider-level helper that *does* honor
  `retry-after`/`retry-after-ms` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai` -> `retryProviderRequest`),
  but it is effectively disabled: `openai-completions` calls it with
  `maxRetries` from `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, which is unset
  (-> 0). The active layer is the agent-level retry in `settings-manager` /
  `agent-session` / `retry.ts`, which ignores the hint. Reuse/extend the
  existing helper rather than adding a third retry path.
- Keep the change minimal; do not regress the completed
  WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO tuning. Note: the installed build observed here still
  shows `baseDelayMs = 2000` (not 7000), so verify version drift before
  assuming that tuning is present.

## Related work

- WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO (completed) - "When a model is loading wait longer before
  retrying" (increased agent retry delays; did **not** add Retry-After honoring).
- llm-proxy startup ramp: LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX (proxy side, `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`).
- llm-proxy `Retry-After` emission: LP-0MPQ2PLTC000GYRZ, LP-0MQS6MPK9000UIZK.

## Out of scope

- The proxy-side startup-ramp behaviour itself (tracked in the llm project).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSWFQU9N002TAOA** – Implement post-persist lifecycle verification with retry (completed)
- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** – Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (completed)
- **WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG** – Same-slot idle tracking for herdr downtime worker (per slot_id) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+166 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac5 (+131 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, active, add, adding, agent (+117 more)

## Summary

Remove the second, competing audit-freshness definition and route every consumer
through the single shared helper.

## Problem

There are two freshness definitions with different semantics:

1. `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`:
   `auditTime > updateTime - AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS` (60 000 ms,
   one-sided).
2. `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `isAuditNotReadyFresh()`:
   `new Date(audit.auditedAt).getTime() >= new Date(itemUpdatedAt).getTime()`
   (strict `>=`, no tolerance) — used by the ordering boost
   (`sortItemsByScore`, `computeScore`, `selectBySortIndex`).

So the icon and downtime dispatcher can call an item fresh while the ordering tier
treats it as stale (or vice versa) — the exact divergence WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE set out
to remove, which only unified the icon and dispatch paths.

## Expected behaviour

- Exactly one freshness definition exists in the codebase.
- The ordering path, the icon path and the dispatch path agree for every input.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditNotReadyFresh` is removed or delegates to the shared `isAuditFresh`.
2. No other file re-implements an `auditedAt` vs `updatedAt` comparison.
3. Symmetric at-or-near semantics are used where intended (`|auditedAt - updatedAt| <
   tolerance`), matching the canonical SorraAgents fix, rather than the current
   one-sided comparison.
4. Tests assert icon, dispatch and ordering agree on: fresh, stale, just-persisted,
   and missing-audit inputs.
5. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- related-to: WL-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents at-or-near canonical fix)

## Summary

Make child-audit coverage explicit so a child covered by a parent audit is not
treated as "no audit" by the icon and the downtime dispatcher.

## Problem

11 of the 12 `completed`/`in_review` items with **no** audit record are children
(e.g. `WL-0MTQ48YKS000PA6H`, `WL-0MU2LF6SZ000JQYI`, `WL-0MU2LFC1Y0077U1U`,
`WL-0MU2LFHBH004VF48`, `WL-0MUAG2S77003JGDL`, `WL-0MTF5WNRB009RHRU`). A parent audit
covers them (child verdicts are reused), but there is no record on the child itself.

Consequences:

- `stageDisplayIcon` falls back to the plain stage icon (no ✅/⏳), so the queue looks
  unaudited.
- `selectAuditCandidate` filters `!isAuditFresh(c.auditedAt, c.updatedAt)`; a child
  with no `auditedAt` is therefore always a candidate, so the downtime worker
  re-dispatches a redundant child audit — which writes and creates more churn.

## Expected behaviour

- A child covered by a parent audit is recorded as covered (inherited/parent audit
  reference or equivalent), and is not re-dispatched or shown as unaudited.
- A child genuinely not covered by any audit is still surfaced for audit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Policy decided and documented: either (a) every child gets its own verdict, or
   (b) a child may record an inherited audit reference to its covering parent audit.
2. If (b): the `audit_results`/work-item model can express an inherited coverage
   reference; `isAuditFresh` (or its caller) treats a covered child as fresh.
3. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` do not dispatch a child already
   covered by a fresh parent audit.
4. `stageDisplayIcon` shows the audit result (or an explicit "covered by parent"
   indicator) for covered children.
5. Tests cover: covered child not dispatched; uncovered child still dispatched;
   parent audit becomes stale → child becomes a candidate again.
6. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- audit skill `SKILL.md` §in-main-slot mode (child-verdict reuse)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `selectAuditCandidate`

Close the gate leak that lets a work item reach `completed`/`in_review` with **no

## Problem

12 of the 52 `completed`/`in_review` items have no audit record. Most are children
closed by propagation, but at least one is a **root-level** item:

   without a fresh audit, unless an explicit waiver is recorded.

   parent/child relationship and age.

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I need the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO traced to a specific
selection path and mechanism, so the fix targets the real code path instead of a hypothesis.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4** (RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement
items). Covers parent **AC1**.

# Context

Planning established that the hypothesis set in the parent description is not sufficient on its own:
the Herdr-head critical-first scan (`selectCriticalFirstCandidates`) only accepts
`status === 'open' || 'blocked'` items, and `dispatchClaimedTier` performs a CAS claim on the
expected `status`+`stage`. A duplicate therefore requires the item to be **genuinely `open` at the
expected stage** at re-dispatch time — i.e. H1 (marker bypass) alone cannot duplicate; H2/H5 (the
item's `status` reverts to `open` while a dispatch pane is still live) is the necessary partner. That
is exactly the scenario the escalation path was built for, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
already documents it ("a previous dispatch was rolled back / the implementing agent aborted and reset
the item to `open` while the standing marker remained").

The incident root log is **not present on this host**: `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
over the five default roots finds no `LP-*` entries at all. AC1 must therefore be satisfied by
targeted instrumentation and reproduction, which AC1 explicitly sanctions.

Also note the second dispatch vector: the coordination leader "validates offers at dispatch-time
without a marker check" (same doc), so the coordination path must be traced too.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1.1 — RED witness.** A characterisation test drives **two idle cycles** in one process against a
critical `plan_complete` (implement-kind) item that is observed `open` at its marker's stage while its
dispatch pane is live, and asserts exactly `1` dispatch. The test **fails** against the pre-fix code
and records the observed dispatch count.

**AC1.2 — Confirmed selection path.** The RCA verdict names the confirmed selection path (Herdr-head
critical-first scan vs coordination offer dispatch) with a source line reference and a cycle-by-cycle
trace (cycle 1: selected/accepted, cycle 2: selected/accepted + claim outcome + marker state).

**AC1.3 — Hypothesis decision table.** Each of H1 (critical-first bypasses marker exclusion), H2
(stale item status in the dispatcher snapshot), H3 (non-atomic rolling-log rewrite), H4 (multiple
leaders) and H5 (item `status` reverted to `open` while a pane is live) is marked **confirmed** /
**refuted** / **not reproducible**, each with the discriminating evidence. H2/H5 is explicitly
confirmed or refuted.

**AC1.4 — Residual uncertainty.** Any hypothesis left open is recorded with the workaround F3/F4
apply for it, and the residual risk is stated.

**AC1.5 — CAS/bypass analysis recorded.** The verdict states whether the duplicate required a real
DB `status: open` (CAS succeeds) or a CAS gap, so F3's guard is justified rather than assumed.

# Minimal implementation

- Add a deterministic two-cycle harness around `dispatchDowntimeWork` using the existing injectable
  seams: `getHerdrListHead`, `getNextItem`, `claimItem`, `spawnAgentPane`, `recordDispatch`,
  `getRunningDowntimePanes`.
- Simulate the live pane via the `herdr pane list` fixture path (`parseHerdrPaneListOutput` /
  `countRunningDowntimePanes`) so the same data shape the dispatcher sees in production is used.
- Simulate the status revert by returning the item as `open` in cycle 2's Herdr head while the marker
  written in cycle 1 stands.
- Capture the per-cycle selection reason (a precursor to the AC6 schema) so the verdict is auditable.
- **Parent AC1 (restated):** The selection path and mechanism that produced the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO are confirmed (H1: critical-first scan bypasses marker exclusion / H2: stale item status in dispatcher snapshot / H3: non-atomic rolling-log rewrite / H4: multiple leaders) via targeted instrumentation or reproduction.

# Dependencies

None. This is the first item in the sequence.

# Deliverables

- RCA verdict comment on parent WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 (decision table + trace + line references).
- New test block in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (the RED witness; promoted to the
  permanent suite by WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB).

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Out of Scope

- Implementing the fix (WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI).
- Multi-leader support (parent out-of-scope).

data.description:
# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the critical-first escalation to skip an item that already has a live
dispatch pane, so a critical item whose `status` reverted to `open` is never dispatched twice, while
escalation of genuinely stuck critical items is preserved.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC2** and **AC3**.

# Design (approved at the plan approval gate)

The critical-first scan currently bypasses the dispatched-marker exclusion **unconditionally**
(WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT). This replaces the unconditional bypass with a **stale-only bypass gated on an
item-scoped live-pane check**, with a marker-TTL fallback when the pane query is unavailable:

```
for a critical-first candidate:
  1. resolve the item-scoped in-flight signal (live dispatch pane whose label suffix is the item id
     and whose agent status is non-terminal)
  2. if a live WORKING pane exists                 -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-pane)
  3. else if the pane query SUCCEEDED and found none -> ESCALATE (reason: no-live-pane)
  4. else (pane query FAILED/unparseable)          -> fall back to the marker TTL:
       fresh marker (age <= markerStaleWindowMs)   -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-unverified)
       stale/absent marker                         -> ESCALATE (reason: marker-stale-escalation)
```

This deliberate **neither-blind-fail-closed-nor-blind-fail-open** choice was confirmed at the approval
gate: escalation is never starved permanently (the TTL fallback keeps progressing), and a duplicate is
never permitted while a pane is live. Note the fallback is benign in practice — pane spawn itself needs
herdr, so a persistent pane-query failure also prevents dispatch.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC2.1 — Live pane blocks.** With a live `working` downtime pane whose label suffix is the item id,
**no** dispatch is attempted for that item — regardless of marker freshness, stage advancement, or
`status` being `open`.

**AC2.2 — Fail-closed on unknown in-flight state.** A failed or unparseable pane query never results in
a dispatch that could duplicate in-flight work; it resolves via the marker-TTL fallback (AC3.3) and
records the `in-flight-unverified` reason.

**AC2.3 — Terminal panes do not block.** Panes whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` do not block
dispatch (no idle-pane deadlock).

**AC2.4 — Item-scoped only.** The guard never uses a global running-pane count as a dispatch limit —
the WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3 invariant is preserved (that count stays a liveness/owner-lease signal only).

**AC2.5 — Normal loop covered.** The guard also applies to critical candidates reaching dispatch
through the normal (non-critical-first) loop, so AC2 holds "regardless of selection path".

**AC3.1 — Escalation preserved.** A critical item with a fresh **or** stale marker and **no** live pane
is still escalated within one idle cycle; all existing critical-first tests stay green.

**AC3.2 — Escalation is bounded.** Deferral happens only while a live working pane exists or while the
marker is fresh during a pane-query outage — never by an unbounded fixed TTL alone.

**AC3.3 — TTL fallback documented.** The fallback bound (`markerStaleWindowMs`, default 24h, floor 1h)
and its rationale are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

# Minimal implementation

- Add an item-scoped in-flight resolver, resolved **once per idle cycle** and threaded into
  `dispatchFromHerdrList`: extend `RunningPanesResult` to expose pane records (or add a sibling dep
  returning `{paneId, itemId, kind, agentStatus}[]`), reusing `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`.
- Derive the item id from the pane label suffix (`buildDowntimePaneTitle` preserves `- <itemId>` as a
  suffix via `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`).
- Replace the critical-first loop's unconditional marker bypass with the decision table above.
- Factor the resolver so WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI can reuse it unchanged (no logic duplication across paths).
- Fail-open on resolver errors in the sense that the resolver returns "unavailable" (never throws into
  the dispatch loop); fail-closed semantics are the decision table's step 4.
- **Parent AC2 (restated):** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.
- **Parent AC3 (restated):** The critical-first escalation path retains its ability to progress items blocked by a stale marker, without re-dispatching in-flight items. Escalation is bounded (e.g., once per claim TTL, or gated on a live-pane / in-flight check).

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB (regression suite — must exist to prove AC5.5's RED→GREEN transition).

# Deliverables

- Code + unit tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` update (§"Critical-first tier & freeze
  split-by-skill").
- RED→GREEN evidence comment referencing the WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB suite.

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the coordination leader to withhold or reject an offer whose item already
has a live dispatch pane, so the coordination path cannot produce the duplicate that the Herdr-head fix
(WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO) prevents.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC2**.

# Context

`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the coordination leader "validates offers at dispatch-time
**without a marker check**". That is a second, independent duplicate-dispatch vector: the Herdr-head fix
alone would leave it open, which is why AC5 names both paths and why this is a separate work item
(decision Q7 at the plan approval gate: keep F3 and F4 separate).

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC2.6 — Offer withheld when in-flight.** An offer for a critical item with a live `working` dispatch
pane is not offered (or is rejected at leader dispatch) and the rejection reason is recorded in the
coordination log.

**AC2.7 — Fallback candidate chosen.** `computeMostImportantItem` does not offer an in-flight critical
item; when another offerable item exists it is chosen instead, and the dispatcher does not fall through
to an empty cycle.

**AC2.8 — Cross-root correctness.** The pane query uses the **offer's own root** (`opts.cwd`), never the
leader pane's root — the WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A cross-root invariant is preserved and asserted.

**AC2.9 — No duplication of logic.** The in-flight resolver is the one factored in WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO; this item
does not reimplement label parsing or pane-status filtering.

**AC2.10 — Leader-side re-check.** Even when an offer was computed before the pane appeared, the
leader's dispatch-time validation rejects it (time-of-check/time-of-use gap closed).

# Minimal implementation

- Resolve the in-flight set for the offer's root inside the offer computation and again at
  leader dispatch time.
- Reuse the WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO resolver; if F3 factored it into a shared helper, import it unchanged.
- Record the withheld/rejected outcome with the reason so it is visible in the coordination log and in
  the AC6 schema.
- **Parent AC2 (restated):** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB (regression suite; F4 does not depend on F3 so the two implementations can run in parallel,
  sharing the resolver).

# Deliverables

- Code + tests in `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` +
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` update.

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the dispatch and coordination rolling logs written atomically, so a
concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log and momentarily lose a
duplicate-dispatch marker.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC4**.

# Context

`appendRollingJsonl` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`) rewrites the log non-atomically: read all
lines → push → trim → `writeFile` directly to the target path. A reader arriving during the
`writeFile` can see a truncated or empty file, which makes `dispatchedItemMarkers` /
`dispatchedItemStages` momentarily lose the marker. This is a contributing factor (H3 in the parent
RCA), not the sole cause — it cannot by itself duplicate a critical-tier item, because the
critical-first scan bypasses markers entirely (that is WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO's fix). It is fixed independently
because it is a genuine TOCTOU defect and because it silently weakens every marker-guarded tier.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC4.1 — Atomic replacement.** `appendRollingJsonl` writes to a temporary sibling file and `rename`s it
over the target. A test asserts the target path is never opened for direct writing.

**AC4.2 — No leaked temp files.** No temporary file remains after a successful append, and none remains
after an I/O failure (cleanup happens before the error is rethrown).

**AC4.3 — Concurrent reader never sees a partial log.** A test that hammers append + read in parallel
observes **only** complete, parseable JSONL lines — never an empty file, never a partial line. The test
fails against the pre-fix writer.

**AC4.4 — Contract unchanged.** Trimming to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (100) and the throw-on-I/O-failure
(fail-closed) contract are unchanged; the file stays human-readable JSONL.

**AC4.5 — Both logs.** Both `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` and the coordination log use the atomic
writer.

**AC4.6 — Same-filesystem rename.** The temp file is created in the same directory as the target so
`rename` is atomic (a cross-device rename would fall back to copy + unlink and lose atomicity).

# Minimal implementation

- Temp file name including pid + random suffix, in the same directory as the target.
- `mkdir(dir, {recursive:true})` unchanged; `readFile`/trim/append logic unchanged; `writeFile` to the
  temp path, then `rename` over the target.
- `try`/`finally`-style cleanup: on any error, best-effort unlink the temp file, then rethrow so the
  caller's fail-closed behaviour (abort the dispatch) is preserved.
- Keep the existing exported signatures so no caller changes are needed.
- **Parent AC4 (restated):** The dispatch and coordination rolling logs use atomic write (write temp file + `rename`) so a concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log.

# Dependencies

None — independently shippable and may land in parallel with WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI.

# Deliverables

- Code + tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Rolling log trimming" update.

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want every dispatcher log entry to record the session/pane id and the selection
path/reason, so the next duplicate-dispatch RCA is answerable from the log alone instead of by
inference.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC6**.

# Context

The current schema is `itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`. Two constraints shape the design:

1. `recordDispatch` runs **before** `spawnAgentPane` (fail-closed ordering: a marker write failure
   aborts the dispatch), and `DowntimeSpawnResult` is `{ok: true}` with no pane id — `send-to-pi.sh` is
   fire-and-forget. The pane/session id is therefore **not** known at marker-write time.
2. `dispatchedItemMarkers` takes the **last** entry per `itemId`, and `markerStillExcludes` is
   fail-closed on a missing/unparseable `dispatchedAt`. Any post-spawn entry must therefore **preserve**
   `dispatchedAt` + `stage` or it would corrupt marker semantics.

Decision at the plan approval gate (Q5): use a **best-effort post-spawn enrichment entry** rather than
extending the spawn contract / `send-to-pi.sh`.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC6.1 — Selection path and reason recorded.** Every successful dispatch entry records
`selectionPath` (e.g. `critical-first` | `normal-scan` | `coordination-offer` | `scheduled-prompt`) and
a machine-readable `selectionReason` (e.g. `marker-stale`, `in-flight-pane`, `no-live-pane`,
`in-flight-unverified`, `non-critical`).

**AC6.2 — Pane/session id recorded without breaking markers.** Successful dispatches record the
resolved pane id via a post-spawn enrichment entry that **preserves** `itemId`, `kind`, `stage` and
`dispatchedAt`; a test round-trips the enriched log through `dispatchedItemMarkers` and
`markerStillExcludes` and proves identical exclusion/release behaviour with and without enrichment.

**AC6.3 — Enrichment is fail-open.** If the pane id cannot be resolved, the dispatch still succeeds and
the log records an explicit absence (no guessed value).

**AC6.4 — Backward compatible.** Legacy entries without the new fields parse and behave exactly as
before; the existing `downtime-log.test.ts` compatibility tests stay green.

**AC6.5 — Tooling reports the new fields.** `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` surfaces
`selectionPath`/`selectionReason`/`paneId` for post-fix evidence (and tolerates their absence).

**AC6.6 — Spawn-failed entries unchanged.** `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries stay non-excluding
(WL-0MT32F908002YFFA AC2 invariant) with or without the new fields.

# Minimal implementation

- Add `selectionPath`, `selectionReason` and an optional `paneId` to `DowntimeDispatchEvent`.
- Thread the selection path/reason from the selection loops (WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ's per-cycle trace provides the
  vocabulary; WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI provide the in-flight reasons).
- After a successful spawn, resolve the pane id (label-suffix lookup against `herdr pane list`) and
  append the enrichment entry, swallowing errors exactly like the existing spawn-failed trace.
- Extend the scan script's output fields and the documented log schema.
- **Parent AC6 (restated):** Each dispatcher log entry records the session/pane id and the selection path/reason, extending the current schema (`itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`) to support automated RCA.

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ (defines the selection-path/reason vocabulary from the confirmed mechanism).

# Deliverables

- Code + tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema update + scan-script field support.

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want reproducible evidence that no new duplicate dispatch occurs after the fix,
so I can trust the fix beyond the test suite and know exactly how to re-verify it.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Provides the observational evidence for parent **AC2**.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC-V1 — Full suite green.** `npm test` passes with WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ's RED witness and WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB's regression
suite GREEN (no skipped or quarantined tests).

**AC-V2 — No new duplicates in the observation window.**
`python3 packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py --since <fix-deploy ISO-8601>` over the five
default roots reports **zero** new duplicate pairs for the dispatch kinds touched by WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO–WL-WL-0MUBVL251006JAQ0
(`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`).

**AC-V3 — Verification is repeatable.** The method, observation window, roots, exact commands and the
resulting JSON report are recorded on the parent item, so the check can be re-run unchanged.

**AC-V4 — Bounded window stated.** The window length is stated together with its limitation (a short
window cannot prove absence of a rare race); the claim is limited to "no observed recurrence in the
window".

**AC-V5 — Test-failure triage.** Any failure found is triaged into a critical `test-failure` work item
via the test skill (`check_or_create.py`) before this item is advanced to `in_review`.

# Minimal implementation

- Run the scan before and after a bounded observation window; capture the JSON report.
- Record the AC6-enriched fields in the report so a future recurrence is diagnosable.
- No production code changes.
- **Parent AC2 (restated):** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO, WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI, WL-WL-0MUBVL1FI0071WN3, WL-WL-0MUBVL251006JAQ0.

# Ship Guard Module — `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`

## Summary
Pure, injectable helper module to guard ship-mode entry by detecting live agent panes working on project work items.

## Parent AC Coverage
This task covers parent ACs 0, 1, 2:
- Parent AC 0: "Pressing the Ship It shortcut (`S`) when one or more **live** agent panes ... does **not** open the Ship It confirmation dialog." — `formatBlockedNotice` and `listBlockingPanes` produce the blocking notice; the guard module enables the pre-dialog gate.
- Parent AC 1: "The blocking check runs **before** the confirmation dialog is rendered." — the guard module returns the blocking set before any dialog logic runs.
- Parent AC 2: "A pane only blocks when it hosts a **live** agent: a pane whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` does not block." — `listBlockingPanes` filters by agent status (not `done`/`exited`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `collectProjectWorkItemIds()` runs `wl list --json` and returns a `Set<string>` of all work-item IDs in the current project's worklog.
- [ ] `listBlockingPanes(projectIds, paneListOutput)` calls `herdr pane list`, extracts work-item IDs from pane labels, filters to panes whose labels carry a project work-item ID and whose agent is live (not `done`/`exited`), and returns the blocking panes.

- [ ] All logic is pure and injectable — no direct file I/O or side effects in the helpers; callers pass command output strings.
- [ ] On query failure (wl list or herdr pane list unavailable), the guard fails safe: listBlockingPanes returns the full set as blocking and the caller must not open the dialog.

# Pre-dialog gate in worklist.ts + Code Freeze on confirm

## Summary
Integrate the ship guard into the worklist's Ship It flow: pre-dialog gate that blocks opening the confirmation dialog when live panes exist, and write the code-freeze marker on confirm before dispatching the release command, with best-effort cleanup on failure.

## Parent AC Coverage
This task covers parent ACs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5:
- Parent AC 0: "Pressing the Ship It shortcut (`S`) ... does **not** open the Ship It confirmation dialog." — guard runs before `openShipItDialog()`; modal notice shown instead.
- Parent AC 1: "The blocking check runs **before** the confirmation dialog is rendered." — guard runs in the chord-resolution branch before any dialog logic.
- Parent AC 2: "A pane only blocks when it hosts a **live** agent." — guard's `listBlockingPanes` filters by live agent status.
- Parent AC 3: "When no blocking pane exists, pressing `S` opens the Ship It confirmation dialog exactly as today." — if guard returns empty, flow continues to `openShipItDialog()`.
- Parent AC 4: "On typing `ship` + Enter, the worklist writes the Code Freeze marker ... **before** dispatching `/skill:ship release`." — `onConfirm` writes marker before `executeResolvedCommand`.
- Parent AC 5: "If dispatching `/skill:ship release` fails, the worklist best-effort removes the Code Freeze marker." — try/catch around dispatch clears marker on failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, the guard runs before `openShipItDialog()`. If blocking panes exist, a modal notice is displayed (listing the panes/work-item IDs) and the dialog is NOT opened.
- [ ] The blocked notice uses the existing in-pane modal notice pattern (like `code-freezeNotice`), dismissible via Esc/Enter/q.
- [ ] In `openShipItDialog`'s `onConfirm` (after user types `ship` + Enter), the code-freeze marker is written **before** calling `executeResolvedCommand(SHIP_IT_COMMAND, ...)`.
- [ ] If dispatching `/skill:ship release` fails (onCommand throws or is a no-op), the marker is best-effort cleared and the error is surfaced to the operator.
- [ ] No regression: when no blocking panes exist, the Ship It dialog opens exactly as before.
- [ ] The typed-confirmation behaviour (case-insensitive `ship`, Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel, bottom-anchored overlay) is unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation
- Modify `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - In the `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` chord-resolution branch, run the guard before `openShipItDialog()`.
  - In `openShipItDialog`'s `onConfirm`, add marker write before dispatch and cleanup on failure.
- Dependencies: `ship-guard.ts` (new), `code-freeze.ts` (extended).

## Deliverables
- Modified `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`

# Measure the post-change benefit of mode-aware AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM

## Problem statement

WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME makes the downtime dispatcher pass a mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` to dispatched audit panes: `2` in cheap mode when a second local slot is genuinely free and the dispatch is single-flight, `1` otherwise. The wiring is live in the running `dev` build (herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38; running checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`) — **no `dev`→`main` release is required** for it to take effect on this machine.

The benefit has not been observed yet. The first post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained no dispatched audits, so the audit-only `PARALLELISM=2` path was never exercised.

This item is the operational follow-up: capture a measurement that actually exercises the path.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants to confirm the change raises cheap-window local slot utilisation without increasing remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-change proxy usage report covering at least one 01:00-10:00 cheap window recorded, and a dispatched audit within that window shown to overlap its Phase 2 children with the parent (peak cheap-mode concurrency 2, not 1).
2. Cheap-window local utilisation compared against the immediate pre-change cheap windows and the 2026-08-22_3 reference, and reported (up, flat, or down). Utilisation is measured by **avg concurrency (while busy) = total compute ÷ busy time** and/or **slot utilisation = total compute ÷ (window × slots)**, not by busy % (which saturates at one busy slot).
3. Remote fallback rate compared against the pre-change rate and reported (must not increase).
4. Dispatched-audit Phase 2 wall-clock (per audit, or median across audits) compared against a pre-change sequential (`PARALLELISM=1`) audit and reported.
5. If the benefit is not observed (utilisation flat/down, or fallback up), a follow-up work item is created with the finding and a proposed remedy.

## Measurement method and baselines

- **Metric.** Busy % (union of ≥1-active-slot intervals ÷ duration) is a coverage/guardrail metric only — it cannot distinguish one busy slot from two. Primary metric: **avg concurrency while busy** and **slot utilisation**; plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap. Both are emitted by the proxy usage report's "Local model utilization" section.
- **Primary baseline — per-audit A/B (best).** The change is audit-only, so the clean comparison is a cheap-mode dispatched audit at `PARALLELISM=2` vs one at `PARALLELISM=1` (matched item, or alternating), comparing Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap per audit.
- **Secondary baseline — immediate pre-change cheap windows** (2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24, 01:00-10:00) for the util/fallback guardrails, normalised for audit and request volume.
- **Reference only — 2026-08-22_3** (`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-22_3/`): 04:00-05:00 38.2%, 05:00-06:00 24.8% busy (the source of the cited "25-38%"); cheap avg concurrency 1.55, peak 4. Same-day runs varied widely (`2026-08-22` 49.9%/55.4%; `_2` 38.2%/55.4%), so a single window is a weak baseline.
- **Data source.** Proxy logs/reports live on the proxy host `192.168.0.199` (`/var/log/llama-proxy`, `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable by SSH from the ContextHub machine. Run the report with an isolated `--output-dir` to avoid disturbing the daily cron outputs.

## Notes

discovered-from:WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME

- Run at least one dispatched audit in a cheap window: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6188a90d HEAD` confirms the code is present; confirm `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` on the audit pane via `/proc/<pid>/environ`.
- Cheap window per the slot schedule is 01:00-10:00.
- This item is operational and assigned to the Operator; it does not block the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME code change. It is blocked on child WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA, which captures a cheap-mode dispatched audit.

# Downtime dispatcher stalls when llama-proxy serves slots:[] + slots_stale:true

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28. Discovered while verifying the parent's AC1 against the LIVE proxy during implementation of the four children.

## Evidence (live proxy, 2026-09-24)

`GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/status`:

```json
{"active_query":true,"local_active_query":true,"model_switch_in_progress":false,"current_model":"Qwen3","llama_server_running":true,"available_slots":1,"total_slots":3,"slots_stale":true,"slots":[],"local_owner_session_id":["http://localhost:8080","herdr-1790261458-1799601-10619"],"local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds":645.5}
```

## Root cause

`parseLlamaStatus` accepts `slots: []` as a valid empty array and ignores the `slots_stale` field entirely. In `tick()`:

- `perSlotMode = Array.isArray(status.slots) && 0 < requiredFreeSlots < total_slots` -> **true** for `slots: []` (an empty array is still an array).
- `perSlotTracker.record([])` starts no timers -> `thresholdMetCount === 0 < requiredFreeSlots` -> `ready === false` -> tick returns `!ready` (idle, no dispatch).
- Even if `ready` were true, `slotOwned = countFreeUnownedSlots([]) === 0` -> true -> refusal.
- `freeSlots = countFreeUnownedSlots([]) = 0`.

When `slots` is absent (not `[]`), the count-based fallback is also blocked: the derived `local_lease_active` is true (owner array + 645 s lease), so `globalIdleChecks` fails.

Result: with `slots: []` / `slots_stale: true` and an active lease, the dispatcher NEVER dispatches — the RCA stall persists despite the child-1 per-slot fix (WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME).

## Proposed fix areas (to be planned)

1. Treat `slots_stale: true` (and/or an empty `slots` array) as "no per-slot identity": parse the flag and fall back to the count-based path.
2. In the count-based path, do not let a lease block dispatch when `available_slots >= requiredFreeSlots` and `total_slots > 1` (spare capacity) — only a truly owned SOLE slot should block.
3. Add a regression test pinned to the exact live payload above.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A payload with `slots: []`, `slots_stale: true`, `total_slots: 3`, `available_slots: 1`, an owner lease and a live dispatched pane dispatches into the free slot(s) (per-slot mode is not entered on stale/empty data).
2. A count-based multi-slot payload with spare `available_slots` and a held lease no longer blocks dispatch.
3. A count-based single-slot payload with a held lease still refuses (preserve WL-0MU8809SZ0022VZG AC3).
4. A contract test pins `slots_stale` parsing and the empty-array fallback.

## Notes

- Blocks the parent RCA's AC1 ("dispatches resume during agent runs").
- Child WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME's comment already anticipated this follow-up ("If cheap-mode responses also serve slots=[] ... perSlotMode is false and the stall persists").
data.title: Downtime dispatcher stalls when llama-proxy serves slots:[] + slots_stale:true (per-slot mode has no identity; count-based fallback lease-blocked)

# Herdr extension crashes at init: TDZ ReferenceError on modeSwitchWorker

## Symptom

Opening the worklist tab (prefix+l) opens the tab but the plugin crashes on initialization:

```
Worklog plugin error: ReferenceError: Cannot access 'modeSwitchWorker' before initialization
    at Object.config (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1611:15)
    at createDowntimeWorker (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:4821:63)
    at main (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1583:42)
```

Reproduced directly: `cd packages/herdr && npx tsx src/index.ts </dev/null` exits 1 with the error above.

## Root cause (temporal dead zone)

- `createDowntimeWorker` calls `opts.config()` SYNCHRONOUSLY during construction (`downtime-worker.ts:4821`, `disableMarkerExists(opts.config().cwd)`).
- The `config` closure passed from `index.ts` evaluates `modeSwitchWorker.getLastKnownMode()` (index.ts:1611).
- `modeSwitchWorker` is declared with `const` **after** `downtimeWorker` (index.ts:1624), so the reference hits the TDZ and throws.

Introduced by the combination of:
- `6188a90d` (WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME) — added the `mode: modeSwitchWorker.getLastKnownMode()` field to the config closure.
- `88a14451` (WL-0MU6MXCZZ007ZXT9) — moved `modeSwitchWorker` creation to AFTER `downtimeWorker`.

There is already a `modeSwitchHolder` declared BEFORE `downtimeWorker` (index.ts:1562) for exactly this kind of forward reference (used by `onProxyIdle`).

## Fix

Use the existing holder in the config closure:

```ts
// index.ts config closure
mode: modeSwitchHolder.worker?.getLastKnownMode() ?? undefined,
```

At construction `modeSwitchHolder.worker` is undefined -> `undefined` (conservative PARALLELISM=1); after `modeSwitchHolder.worker = modeSwitchWorker` is assigned, later ticks read the real mode. No TDZ.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `npx tsx src/index.ts` no longer throws "Cannot access 'modeSwitchWorker' before initialization" / "Worklog plugin error" at startup.
2. Mode-aware Phase 2 parallelism is preserved: once the mode-switch worker exists, `config().mode` returns its last-known mode.
3. A regression test guards the plugin startup path (no TDZ / no init crash).
4. Build + full test suite green; commit pushed to dev.
data.title: Herdr extension crashes at init: TDZ ReferenceError on modeSwitchWorker in downtime config()

The herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) does not compile at `dev` HEAD (`227cbe11`). `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1920` uses the type `PaneLifecycleKind` in the `closePane` dependency signature, but the type is never imported, producing:

```
src/downtime-worker.ts(1920,40): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'PaneLifecycleKind'.
```

## User story

As a developer working from `dev`, I want the herdr plugin to build cleanly after a pull, so I am not blocked by a compile error.

## Root cause

- `PaneLifecycleKind` is defined and exported in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts:110`.
- The reference was introduced by commit `24b1e575` (`WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN: implement auto-close logic with implement exception`).
- `git log --all -S "type PaneLifecycleKind" -- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` returns no commit: the import has never existed in any commit.
- It escaped notice because root `npm run build` compiles root `src/**/*` only — `packages/herdr` is not part of the root tsconfig, and the plugin's own `npm run build` is not wired into the root build/postbuild or CI.

Note: a separate set of `isAuditFresh` "Expected 2 arguments, but got 4" errors can appear on a stale checkout; those are caused by an outdated copied `packages/herdr/node_modules/@worklog/shared` and are resolved by refreshing the shared build — they are not source defects. This item is scoped to the genuine missing-import regression only.

## Discovered from

`WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN` (introduced the missing reference).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` imports `PaneLifecycleKind` from `./downtime-log.js` (type-only, consistent with the existing type imports in that block).
2. `npm run build` inside `packages/herdr` succeeds with zero `tsc` errors against a freshly-built `@worklog/shared`.
3. A regression guard test (part of the root vitest suite) runs `tsc --noEmit` for the `packages/herdr` project and asserts it exits 0, so an unimported type can never again ship unnoticed.
4. Root `npm run build` still succeeds (no regression).

## Out of scope

- Wiring `packages/herdr` build into the root build/CI (record as a follow-up work item if desired).
- Fixing local `node_modules` staleness.

# Interview: LLM-Assisted Question Extraction

**Headline:** When `wl interview <id>` finds no parseable questions using the deterministic parser, optionally invoke a local LLM (via the existing embedding infrastructure) to extract unanswered questions from the description in free text.

## Problem Statement

The deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection` + `parseQAPairs`) requires an exact section header and rigid formatting. Real work items use varied formats (e.g., `## Appendix: Clarifying questions \& answers` with `- **Q1**: "..." — Answer (user@...): "..."). As a result, zero of the 17 `needsProducerReview=true` items are currently detectable. The original audit rejected WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 stating: "The command does not reliably detect questions."

An LLM normaliser turns this hard format dependency into a soft one — it can extract questions regardless of prose format.

## Users

- **Producers** running `wl interview <id>` — they want the command to find questions even when the description doesn't follow the canonical format.
- **Developers** — they want the feature to work with local models (Ollama/Foundry), not require a cloud API key.

**User Story:** "As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they're written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the deterministic parser finds no questions, and the `--llm` flag is set (or `intelligent: true` in config), the command calls a local LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible embedding infrastructure `src/lib/search.ts`.
2. The LLM is asked to return a JSON array of `{ question: string }` objects extracted from the description, or an empty array if none found.
3. Each extracted question is presented to the user interactively (same `createPromptLoop` readline flow) for confirmation and answer.
4. Only confirmed questions are written to the description using the **deterministic re-serialiser** (`rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`) — never written directly from LLM output.
5. When no LLM is available (no config, network failure, timeout), the command falls back to the existing deterministic-only message with no error.
6. The LLM call is bounded: description is truncated to 8 KB, a timeout of 15 seconds is enforced.
7. Tests cover: mock client returns valid questions, mock returns empty, mock throws error, no config available, timeout.

## Configuration

Opt-in via one of:
- `--llm` CLI flag: `wl interview <id> --llm`
- Config file: `intelligent: true` under `interview` section in `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Constraints

- No new dependencies — reuse `src/lib/search.ts` embedding infrastructure (OpenAI-compatible client, config resolution, graceful degradation).
- LLM is a *text completion* client, not an embedding client — but the same provider config, base URL, model, and auth apply. We should either:
  - (a) Add a `llm.*` config section parallel to `embedding.*`
  - (b) Or reuse the same provider config (the embedder already supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- The deterministic parser remains the primary path; LLM is strictly a fallback.
- Output is interactive-only (no --json mode for LLM calls).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — New `--llm` option, LLM client invocation, user confirmation loop for extracted questions.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Add `llm?: boolean` to `InterviewOptions`.
- `src/lib/search.ts` — Potentially add a `ChatClient` class alongside the existing `OpenAIEmbedder`, or reuse its config resolution for a completion client.
- `src/config.ts` — Add `interview.llm` or `llm.*` config schema.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — New test cases for LLM path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Model availability:** Not all setups have an LLM configured. Fallback must be silent and graceful.
- **Cost:** One completion call per invocation (~2-3 KB input) is cheap even at $0.001/call, but should be bounded.
- **Hallucination:** The mandatory user-confirmation step before writing to the description mitigates this.
- **Scope creep risk:** Users may want batch extraction across multiple items or LLM-generated answers. Track separately.
data.title: interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback

# Capture a cheap-mode dispatched audit to measure Phase 2 PARALLELISM benefit

discovered-from:WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5

## Finding

The mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` code is live in the running `dev` build
(herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38 and contains the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME wiring;
the running checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`). A `dev`→`main` release is
**not** required for the change to take effect.

The first full post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained **no
dispatched audits** — the downtime dispatcher selected only implement/plan/intake/
scheduled items (last audit dispatch was 2026-09-24T23:54Z in fast mode; no
`audit-*` pi sessions started in the window). Because the `PARALLELISM=2` path is
audit-only, it was never exercised, so the Phase 2 benefit is unmeasured.

Window-level metrics (proxy host 192.168.0.199): remote fallback 41.7% post vs 52.8%
pre; cheap busy 67.7% both; **avg concurrency while busy 1.72 post vs 1.46 pre**;
total compute 9h 39m post vs 7h 43m pre (both confounded by differing workload).

## Goal

As the operator, I want at least one dispatched audit to run during a cheap window so I
can measure whether mode-aware `PARALLELISM=2` makes its Phase 2 children overlap the
parent and shortens Phase 2 wall-clock, without raising remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At least one dispatched audit runs in a 01:00-10:00 cheap window, and
   `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` is confirmed on the audit pane (e.g. via
   `/proc/<pid>/environ`).
2. **Primary (per-audit A/B):** the cheap-mode `PARALLELISM=2` audit's Phase 2 wall-clock
   and child overlap (peak concurrency 2 during Phase 2) are compared against a
   `PARALLELISM=1` audit — matched item, or alternating — and reported.
3. **Secondary (window guardrails):** cheap-window **avg concurrency (while busy)** and
   **slot utilisation (total compute ÷ window × slots)** are compared against the
   immediate pre-change cheap windows (2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24, 01:00-10:00),
   normalised for audit/request volume, and reported.
4. Remote fallback rate does not increase vs the pre-change comparison.
5. Findings recorded on WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5.

## Proposed remedy (pick one)

- Prefer audit-tier work items for downtime dispatch during cheap windows, so the new
  path is exercised; or
- Trigger one manual cheap-window audit and capture the spawn env plus the proxy report;
  or
- Extend the observation period until a dispatched audit lands in cheap mode.

## Notes

- **Do not use busy % as the success metric** — it saturates at one active slot and is
  blind to the second cheap slot the change is meant to use. Use avg concurrency /
  slot utilisation plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock. Busy % and fallback are guardrails.
- Reference-only baseline: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-22_3/` (04:00-05:00 38.2%,
  05:00-06:00 24.8% busy; cheap avg concurrency 1.55, peak 4). Same-day variance of the
  2026-08-22 runs was large, so window metrics alone are weak evidence.
- Proxy logs/reports live on 192.168.0.199 (`/var/log/llama-proxy`,
  `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable over SSH. Use an isolated `--output-dir` when
  re-running the report.

data.comment:
Root cause of the rejected audit found: users write `--fields id, title` with a space after the comma. The shell splits that into separate argv tokens, so Commander assigned only "id," to `--fields` and treated the trailing token as the positional search/query argument (silently dropping any further fields). That is why "when id is included only id is returned" and "when omitted the requested fields are returned with the id".

Fix (commit 41e46e6d): normalizeFieldsArgv() merges space-separated `--fields` continuations before Commander parses argv. It only merges when the accumulated value ends with a comma, so a complete `--fields id,title` followed by a positional search/query term is unaffected. The `-f` shorthand is scoped to list/search because `-f` also means `--file` on export/import/migrate/sync/doctor.

Verified the shipped artifact: `wl list --fields title, status` now returns id, title and status. Tests added: unit tests for normalizeFieldsArgv (11) and integration tests for space-separated fields on list and search. Full suite passes.

data.comment:
## RCA — why the original fix didn't work (producer rejection NL)

Producer rejection (recovered from the herdr command log): *"This doesn't seem to work, I'm seeing the local retry mechanism overriding the recommended wait duration. Take a look in the logs to see if there is evidence of this happening. If there is then RCA and fix."*

### Evidence

Scanned all Pi session journals (`.pi/agent/sessions/`): **435** `503 startup_ramp` errors. Every single one has this exact assistant error message shape, with **no `retry_after` field**:

    503: {"type":"startup_ramp","code":"startup_ramp","message":"Server is starting up; retry shortly."}

Reconstructed retry gaps from session `herdr-1789911496-958088-22373` (AI_Hell, 2026-09-20): `+2.4s / +4.2s / +9.2s / +16.1s / +32.3s / +60.3s / +60.3s` — i.e. the local exponential schedule, ignoring the proxy's recommended wait.

### Root cause

1. The original fix parsed the retry hint from the assistant **error message** (`parseServerRetryDelayMs`). Real startup-ramp errors never contain `retry_after`; the hint is only on the **HTTP `Retry-After` header**.
2. Pi's `openai-completions` provider (the Local Proxy's API) throws on the non-2xx response *before* the `after_provider_response` extension event fires, and `formatProviderError` renders only `<status>: <body>` — the header value is dropped before the extension ever sees it.
3. Therefore `parseServerRetryDelayMs()` returned `undefined` for every real ramp error, and the loop fell back to plain exponential backoff — exactly the producer's observation.

### Fix

- New `createRetryHintCapturingFetch()` — a transparent `globalThis.fetch` wrapper installed at recovery registration. It records `Retry-After` / `Retry-After-Ms` from 429/5xx responses and clears the hint on 2xx. This is the only point where the header is observable for `openai-completions`; it sits inside `proxy-sse-signals`'s capturing fetch (which reads `globalThis.fetch` at call time).
- New `parseRetryAfterHeaders()` parses the captured header (delta-seconds, `retry-after-ms`, HTTP-date; `Headers` or plain record).
- `resolveRetryDelay()` now takes a `headerHintMs` argument that **takes precedence** over the error-message hint, and reports `hintSource` (`header` | `message`).
- The error-message parse is retained as a fallback (AC2) for providers that fold the hint into the text.
- `installFetchRetryHintCapture()` is called from `registerRecoveryModule()`; `triggerInvisibleContinue()` passes the captured hint into `resolveRetryDelay()`.

The retry loop remains the single retry layer (AC7): the fetch wrapper only observes, it does not retry.

### Scope note (deviation, still flagged for producer)

The brief's constraint says the change belongs in the Pi coding agent codebase. That source checkout is not available in this environment (no `/home/rgardler/projects/pi-coding-agent`; the installed pi is a root-owned bundle with no `src/`). The fix therefore lands in the Worklog recovery module — the layer that actually performs the observed `2/4/8/16/32/60` retries (it suppresses pi's built-in `_prepareRetry`).

data.comment:
## Post-implementation log verification (2026-09-25): clients still do NOT honour Retry-After

Investigated whether clients now respect the proxy's retry instruction. **They do not.** Evidence from proxy and client logs.

### Proxy IS emitting the hint
`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, mode-switch drain gate (ui.py) returns 503 with both `Retry-After` header and top-level body `retry_after`:
- 2026-09-25 13:13:17.268 `Deferring chat request during mode-switch drain (retry_after=44s)`
- 2026-09-25 13:13:19.291 (retry_after=42s), 13:13:23.304 (38s), 13:13:31.327 (30s)

### Client is ignoring it
Client session `herdr-1790338396-3843403-13820` (09-25, after fix commit 5ccc2ae3) hit the drain. The folded assistant error is:
`503: {"type":"mode_switch_drain","code":"mode_switch_drain","message":"Mode switch in progress; retry shortly."}`
Retry gaps remain the old exponential pattern, independent of the 44/42/38s hints: **+2.0s, +4.0s, +8.0s (+16.0s)**.

Same pattern in post-fix sessions:
- 2026-09-22 09:07:11 — gaps +2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0
- 2026-09-23 15:44:38 — gaps +2.1 / +4.0 / +8.0
- 2026-09-25 13:13:17 — gaps +2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0

Across ALL client session journals, no assistant `errorMessage` ever contains `retry_after`/`Retry-After`.

### Root cause — the fix parses a surface the hint never reaches
1. Proxy body is `{"error":{...},"status":503,"retry_after":N}` plus `Retry-After` header.
2. `openai` SDK v6.40.0 (`src/core/error.ts` `APIError.generate`) does `const error = errorResponse?.['error'];` — it keeps only the inner `error` object and discards the top-level `retry_after`/`status` (header IS retained on `error.headers`).
3. pi-ai 0.87.x `normalizeProviderError`/`pickBodyText` stringifies only `error.error` into `errorMessage` → `503: {inner object}`; headers are not folded in.
4. The Worklog extension's `parseServerRetryDelayMs()` (AC1/AC2) parses `errorMessage`, which contains no hint → returns undefined → falls back to `calculateDelay()` exponential backoff, no jitter.
5. pi-ai's provider-level `retryProviderRequest` DOES read `error.headers.get('retry-after')`, but remains disabled (`maxRetries: 0`; `retry.provider.maxRetries` unset).

### Conclusion
AC1/AC2 are NOT met in practice (unit tests pass because they feed a synthetic error string containing the hint, which the real pipeline never produces). AC5 (jitter) is therefore also not exercised. This is consistent with the existing manual audit rejection (2026-09-23).

Remediation options (out of scope here, for a follow-up): (a) enable provider-level `retry.provider.maxRetries` so pi-ai honours the header directly, or (b) surface `Retry-After`/`retry_after` into `errorMessage` (or expose headers to the extension), or (c) have the proxy put the numeric hint inside the `error` object (e.g. `error.retry_after`) so it survives SDK folding.

data.comment:
## RCA — why the previous fix still did not work

Re-read the producer's rejection and the herdr-downtime RCA (`WL-C0MUG2D1JI00581HX`). The previous fix correctly added `Retry-After` header capture via a transparent `globalThis.fetch` wrapper, but left the delay decision as `floor = max(exponential, serverHintMs)`.

That `max()` is the defect behind *"the local retry mechanism overriding the recommended wait duration"*: once the local exponential outgrows the server hint, it silently overrides it. With the proxy's ramp hints of 5-18s, the effective schedule still becomes:

| attempt | local exponential | Retry-After | `max()` delay (jitter 0) |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | 2s | 7s | 7s |
| 2 | 4s | 7s | 7s |
| 3 | 8s | 7s | 8s |
| 4 | 16s | 7s | **16s** |
| 5 | 32s | 7s | **32s** |
| 6 | 60s | 7s | **60s** |

So the header is captured, but the local backoff still governs from attempt 4 onward — the client waits *longer* than the server asked, ignoring the hint.

### Fix

When a usable server hint is present it is now **authoritative**: `delay = min(hint * (1 + jitter), maxDelayMs)`. The local exponential backoff applies **only** when the hint is absent/malformed (AC3 unchanged). Upward-only jitter (AC5) and the configurable cap (AC1) are preserved.

### Verification

- The hint-derived delay no longer escalates with the attempt number.
- Missing/malformed hints still produce the original exponential schedule.
- Full-ramp survival (AC4) unchanged (the loop has no retry budget).

Measurement-plan decision applied (operator approved, "as you recommend").

## 1. Metric corrected

Busy % (union of "≥1 local slot generating" intervals ÷ duration) is a coverage/guardrail metric: it saturates at 100% with a single busy slot, so it cannot detect the change's intended effect (filling the second cheap slot). Success will be measured by, from the report's **Local model utilization** section:

- **avg concurrency (while busy)** — total compute ÷ busy time (e.g. 2026-09-25 1.72 vs 2026-09-24 1.46), and
- **slot utilisation** — total compute ÷ (window × slots) (e.g. 53.6% vs 42.9% for the 9h cheap windows),
- plus **per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap** (the actual claim).

Busy % and remote fallback remain guardrails. AC2/AC5 reworded accordingly.

## 2. Baselines tiered

- **Primary — per-audit A/B (best):** cheap-mode dispatched audit at `PARALLELISM=2` vs `PARALLELISM=1` (matched/alternating); compare Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap per audit. This is the only comparison that isolates an audit-only change.
- **Secondary — immediate pre-change cheap windows:** 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 01:00-10:00, normalised for audit/request volume.
- **Reference only — `2026-08-22_3`:** this is the true source of the cited 25-38% (04:00-05:00 38.2%, 05:00-06:00 24.8%). The other same-day runs differ materially (`2026-08-22` 49.9%/55.4%; `_2` 38.2%/55.4%), so a single window is a weak baseline.

## 3. Empirically observed post-change values (first window)

2026-09-25 01:00-10:00: avg concurrency 1.72 (vs 1.46 pre), total compute 9h 39m (vs 7h 43m), fallback 41.7% (vs 52.8%) — directionally favourable, but **not attributable to the change** because no audit was dispatched and workload volume differed (1970 vs 2821 requests). Hence AC1/AC4 remain unmet and a cheap-mode dispatched audit is still required.

## 4. Disposition

- Parent ACs and description revised; child **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** revised to the per-audit A/B + utilisation plan and remains the blocker.
- Both reset to `open`, assignee Operator.
- Note: the earlier claim that a `dev`→`main` release was required is corrected in the description — the change is already live from `dev`.
